Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just keep it to the accident details, if that's alright. I'm the driver of the vehicle involved.
Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where the incident happened?
A: It was on a multi-lane road in Pasadena, Texas, heading toward the freeway on-ramp. I was moving over one lane
to get into the right-hand lane.
Q: What time of day was it, and what were the road conditions?
A: Mid-afternoon, I think. It was dry, no rain. Traffic was moderate, not stopped.
Q: Walk me through what happened when you changed lanes.
A: I checked my mirror, saw nothing right beside me, and signaled. I started drifting over slowly. Then I felt a bump on
my driver's side and heard scraping. The other car had come up into my blind spot, I guess, and we sideswiped each
other.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before you moved over?
A: Not that I recall. I looked, but it wasn't in my mirror when I checked.
Q: Did either of you stop after contact?
A: Yes, we both pulled onto the shoulder a short way down the road and got out to look at the damage.
Q: Were you hurt?
A: Yes, my right shoulder took the brunt of it when I jerked the wheel. It's sore and I've had trouble lifting my arm
above my head since then. I saw a doctor afterward.
Q: Did you need any emergency assistance at the scene?
A: The police came and filed a report. An ambulance wasn't needed, but I went to urgent care later that day.
Q: Is there anything else you think I should know?
A: Only that I've been careful about my driving and I want to get my vehicle repaired and my shoulder checked out
properly.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
A: Okay, thank you.
</page>
